doc.title: Art Farmer — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Oscar Pettiford's big band
summary: Working with Benny Golson in Pettiford's twelve-piece band and its personnel.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Could one look at this as perhaps the impetus to form the group that you did with Benny?

That was part of it. Prior to forming the Jazztet, Benny had left the Jazz Messengers and was living in New York. We had run into each other on various other gigs. We worked together with a band that was led by Oscar Pettiford, a great bassist…
Excuse me, who else was in that band?

Sahib Shihab was on baritone. Jerome Richardson was in the band. There was a very fine trumpet player named Ray Copeland. James Cleveland was in the band. It wasn’t like a sixteen piece band. Maybe it was like twelve pieces or something like that, I can’t remember everyone’s name. Hank Jones was there. Oscar was one of the monumental bassists in the history of jazz. Joe Harris was playing drums or else Osie Johnson playing drums. It was a good band, it was a positive experience really.
Did you work much? I mean, big bands in the late fifties…
No, not much, but he had a deal to work in Jazzland so many weeks a year. Not Jazzland, I mean Birdland [laughs]. Excuse me.
